item.title: Ken Paxton sues networking company, alleging links with Chinese Communist Party
item.description: AUSTIN (KXAN) -- Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton filed a lawsuit against networking company TP-Links System Inc. alleging it deceived marketing its devices and allowed the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) to access American consumers' devices in their homes.

item.title: Austin Police name suspect, victim of Valentine's Day murder
item.description: Austin Police on Tuesday identified two people whom officers found dead at a residence on Valentine's Day, and said one stabbed the other before taking his own life.

item.title: Abbott votes early, tells Texans it's 'a great day to go out and vote'
item.description: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott spoke to media in Austin Tuesday morning after voting early in the state's primary election.

item.title: $25 million expansion planned for Texas State's ALERRT Training Center
item.description: The Texas State University System Board of Regents has approved a $25 million expansion of the ALERRT Center, a nationally-recognized training facility that prepares first responders to handle active shooter situations and other violent threats.

item.title: Gov. Abbott says districts may lose daily attendance funding over anti-ICE walkouts
item.description: At an early voting news conference Tuesday, Texas Governor Greg Abbott talked about recent school walkouts and ways the state may take action against schools, districts and educators.

item.title: Clouds to sunshine and 80s continues until Friday
item.description: More clouds and a weak front on Friday morning will knock temperatures back into the 70s. Some areas of drizzle will be possible too. -- Nick Bannin

item.title: $100 million increase in federal funding for Alzheimer's, dementia research signed into law
item.description: Advocates for Alzheimer's and dementia research applauded a $100 million increase in funding, approved by Congress and signed by the president earlier this month.

item.title: Austin ISD to manage special ed without state oversight for first time in nearly three years
item.description: Texas Education Commissioner Mike Morath on Tuesday is telling Austin ISD leaders he will removing the two state-appointed monitors who have overseen AISD ever since 2023 when a state investigation found the district repeatedly missed strict state and federal deadlines for evaluating kids suspected of needing special education services.

item.title: Texas GOP AG candidates to face off in Dallas debate
item.description: Republican candidates for Texas Attorney General will meet Tuesday night on stage in Dallas for a primary debate.

item.title: With more than 900 complaints about Texas HOAs, what the state can learn from others about resolving issues
item.description: Community associations in Texas have been criticized for their lack of transparency and increased fees, leading to frustration among residents, while state lawmakers are pushing for more oversight and regulation.
